current_commit_implementation: Public Integral substitution respects flat nested scopes, indefinite coordinate renaming, primitive evaluation limits, exact symbol identities and explicit unknown-function dependencies.
Integral(f, (x, point)) and integrate(f, (x, point)) evaluate supported primitives; unknown primitives retain the original point and remaining limits.
Native single-point Integral differentiation applies chain and parameter rules with exact coordinate identity.
Simultaneous substitutions use compound opaque placeholders restored in one structural pass; evaluated literal zero/infinity and literal NaN products reuse the public nan singleton.
Literal folding admits exact native numeric/constant atoms only; held, symbolic, opaque and composite original-source domain trees retain their existing paths.

Final independent review replaced arbitrary numerator export with native Integer/Rational zero comparisons, retaining raw rational-zero coverage without imposing the Python integer-conversion ceiling on multiplication.
